name: Snatch Back Splash AI: Steal It Back and Splash a Three
blurb: Snatch Back Splash is the AI version of a viral snatch back basketball clip from October 2026: a player gets mad low on the snatch back, rips the ball back from the defender, pulls up and splashes a three.

prompts.label: 1. The video prompt is filled in. Settings: Seedance 2.5, 15 s, 720p, 9:16, sound on. The video prompt
prompts.text:
A photorealistic clip from a live pro basketball game filmed from the courtside seats on a long telephoto lens: on a light-maple court, the person in [Image 1], wearing exactly the clothes from their photo instead of a jersey, bends down extremely low and snatches the ball back off the dribble of a defender in a plain white jersey, who stumbles forward off balance. Warm arena light, slightly muted film colour, natural grain. No captions, no scoreboard graphics.

One continuous handheld vertical 9:16 take from the front row, no cuts. The long lens follows the player, full body and large in the frame, and only whips up with the ball to the rim, then drops back.

The player is the person in [Image 1], in every frame: copy the exact face from [Image 1] (the face shape, eye color and eye shape, eyebrows, nose, mouth, skin tone, age, hair color, hair length and hairstyle, and any beard, moustache, glasses or freckles), the same build, and the clothes and shoes from [Image 1], never a jersey. An adult. The same face from the first frame to the last, so their friends recognize them at once. Never morph. If [Image 1] shows an animal, the player is that animal upright on its hind legs, with its own face, fur and markings, not a person.

The place: a packed pro arena at a night game, plain navy and green court lines, no logo at center court, a courtside front row of adult fans behind the sideline. Teammates in plain navy jerseys, defenders in plain white jerseys.

0-3 s: the player brings the ball up past center court.
3-6 s: at the top of the arc the player faces one defender in white, sinks low and wide and dribbles between the legs.
6-7.5 s: the player drives; the defender pokes the ball loose and takes off with it.
7.5-9 s: the snatch back: the player gets down extremely low, almost to the floor, and rips the ball right back; the defender stumbles forward.
9-10.5 s: two quick dribbles back behind the three-point line, then the player rises and shoots a three.
10.5-12 s: the camera whips up with the ball in a high arc over the crowd; it drops clean through the net, a splash.
12-15 s: the camera drops back: the player backpedals up the court, cool, with a small nod, face sharp and turned to the camera, while the courtside fans jump up and cheer.

The ball's path: in the player's hands from 0 to 6.5 s, in the defender's hands from 6.5 to 8 s, back in the player's hands from 8 s, released at 10.5 s, through the net at 11.5 s.

Audio: arena sound from the stands: sneakers, the ball bouncing, a rising "oh, oh, oh" from the fans at the steal, a big cheer at the splash. No background music, no lyrics, no commentary. No dialogue throughout the entire video.

Exactly one ball. No logos, team names, player names, readable numbers, words on boards, captions or watermark. No famous athlete: every other player and fan is a generic adult. One head, two arms, two legs, five fingers on each hand; the player never merges with the defender or the ball.
